tasks.title: Concurrent cell prepares keep invalidating each other's readiness validation
tasks.notes: NEEDS USER INPUT (design choice). Seen 2026-10-31 on Portswood Rec (53,-42) with neighbour sessions preparing 52,-42/52,-43: `prepare --apply` on one cell changed the readiness revision of neighbouring cells, so a separate prepare then apply was refused 'validation stale' four times; builders had to chain prepare && apply in one shell command. Revision = content_id([POLICY, facts revision, plan_identity]) in lib/journal/cell_readiness.py; I did not find which input changes (suspect vector-map extract rewrite or neighbour plan notes). Questions: should validation of cell A depend on neighbour state at all? Should apply refresh validation itself under the lock? Decide, then fix.

tasks.title: prepare --apply records a duplicate plan_feature on every run (ambiguous legacy plan warning)
tasks.notes: NEEDS USER INPUT. On 53,-42 repeated `prepare --apply` added a second plan `houses_brickfield_road` for the same 6 houses already planned as houses_brickfield_road_w176633174, with warning 'ambiguous legacy plan ... no readable handoff spec'; a duplicate `houses_kitchener_road` (bare id from the 2026-10-29 build in row -43) also showed planned in 53,-42. I dismissed both with dismiss-feature. Decide whether prepare should skip groups already covered by a spec-backed plan, and how legacy bare ids should be matched.

tasks.title: Feature builds across a cell edge silently invalidate a finished neighbour and may generate ghost cells
tasks.notes: NEEDS USER INPUT (policy). Applying houses_kitchener_road_w176634502 (footprint z -5382..-5343) reached 5 blocks into finished cell 53,-43 and marked its trees/decor stale (trees=False, decor=False). An earlier apply also generated a lidar ghost cell at 56,-40 (230k blocks, 'ghost-ground' journal seq 620) that the user did not ask for. Decide: warn/confirm before an apply touches a done neighbour; keep or drop frontier ghost generation on feature applies; whether edge fringe (roof overhang) should invalidate trees/decor at all.

tasks.title: reapply_feature refuses legacy house builds with no recorded builder; house_build apply bypasses the guard
tasks.notes: NEEDS USER INPUT. houses_kitchener_road_w176658416 could not be reapplied (reapply_feature: no available recorded builder). At the owner's request I applied its old spec directly with house_build.py --apply under the lock (31905 positions, 0 mismatches), which bypasses the legacy-builder refusal and still leaves no recorded builder. Decide whether to backfill builder records for legacy spec-backed features (links #225, #228) so reapply works, and whether direct spec apply should be allowed for them.

tasks.title: World provider osm_extract.py: ogr2ogr ran without OSM_CONFIG_FILE; duplicates lib/sources
tasks.notes: NEEDS USER INPUT. In worlds/southampton-build/providers/geofabrik-hampshire/osm_extract.py run_ogr2ogr passed no --config OSM_CONFIG_FILE, so GDAL 3.13's default schema (no `amenity` on points) failed the furniture preset and blocked `prepare --apply`. I patched it in the world checkout (osm_config(): world downloads/osmconf.ini else TOOL_ROOT/config/osmconf.ini); the patch is uncommitted and has no test, on top of the owner's existing uncommitted edits. The world provider duplicates the presets and run_ogr2ogr in lib/sources/geofabrik_provider.py; decide whether to delete the copy and call the tool one. Also: manifest hints from prepare (`ref_manifest.py add ...` for prepared-53--42 and prepared-54--42, 52,-42, 52,-43) were not run.

tasks.title: Background cell sessions downloaded aerial tiles without authorization
tasks.notes: NEEDS USER INPUT (process). The session for cell 52,-42 downloaded 10 Google z19 tiles (1.47 MB, reference/aerial/cell-52-42-z19/) although its brief said downloads were not authorized; the owner then approved keeping them. AGENTS/cell-orchestrator say tile downloads need stated source, filename, size and human authorization. Decide whether google_aerial/prepare tooling should enforce an explicit authorization flag rather than rely on briefs.

tasks.title: Trial: railway run with real rails in a study area (owner picks the stretch)
tasks.notes: NEEDS USER INPUT: the owner names the world and the stretch, and says whether it may be rebuilt. Plan: docs/plans/vibe-at-scale.md sections 5 and 6. Owner idea 2026-11-10: real Minecraft rails for long runs of railway, with land height and direction hacking. This is a spike: the deliverable is findings plus a throwaway prototype, not a production builder. Stretch: at least 300 blocks with a curve and a cutting or embankment. Steps: (1) get the railway lines for the area (railway is not in CELL_EXTRACT_LAYERS today; state where they come from, for example a one-off extract from the world's OSM provider) and snap the centreline to a rail-legal path (long cardinal runs, 90-degree corners, diagonals as staircases); (2) take a lidar ground profile along it, smooth and clamp to a gentle gradient (find the real-world figure from a source and cite it), level the corridor with cut or fill and grass side slopes; (3) lay ballast and rails, with one ascending rail only where a step is needed; (4) apply under the site lock with a structure backup and look in game with the owner. First version leaves out bridges, tunnels, road crossings, fences, stations and signals; note where each would be needed. The prototype lives in the scratchpad, or on a task/* branch only if the owner wants to keep it. Game rules to confirm on the current client: rail needs a solid block below, slopes only on straight cardinal runs at 1 block per block, curves flat, diagonals as staircases. Deliver findings in docs/plans/railway.md: what looked right and wrong, blocks changed outside the corridor, minutes and session tokens used (method stated), and a recommendation with the follow-up implementation tasks to file from the findings. Scratch effects and any snags go to the named world's repo; standing up a new world is separate world work. Check: findings file has a Cost heading and table rows; the owner's in-game verdict on whether the run reads as a railway and the corridor looks natural is recorded in it.

tasks.title: Trial: rule-built typology buildings versus per-building specs (owner picks terrace, estate and shop parade)
tasks.notes: NEEDS USER INPUT: the owner names the world and three study streets, and says whether they may be rebuilt. Plan: docs/plans/vibe-at-scale.md sections 2 and 6. Today houses use scripts/house_build.py (already a rule-based footprint builder with a small spec) and non-house buildings use a full hand-written spec in site/builds/<name>.json built by feature_build.py. Question: how much of a real district can rules cover well, using footprint, lidar height, OSM tags (building, building:levels, roof:shape) and a small per-district choice of palette and roof form. This is a spike. The prototype generates minimal specs for the existing builders (house_build and feature_build); it does not add a third builder. Baseline is house_build with a minimal spec versus a full feature_build spec for the same buildings. Study streets: a terrace, a semi-detached or detached estate street, a shop parade. Build about 20 buildings per street with the prototype and compare with the current path, noting minutes and session tokens per building (method stated) and what the player sees from the street. Pitched roofs use pitched_roof_states as it is today. Deliver findings in docs/plans/typology-buildings.md: which building classes the rules cover, what still needs a designer, cost per building under each path, and a recommendation, including whether roof and facade detail (I-006) and glazing become class recipes. File implementation tasks from the findings, not before. Scratch effects and snags go to the named world's repo. Check: findings file has a Cost heading and table rows; the owner's in-game verdict on whether the rule-built streets read as the real ones is recorded in it.

tasks.title: Trial: industrial estate, retail park and high street (owner picks study areas)
tasks.notes: NEEDS USER INPUT: the owner names the world, an industrial estate or retail park and a high street, and says whether they may be rebuilt. Plan: docs/plans/vibe-at-scale.md section 6. Owner direction 2026-11-10: the world will need industrial and commercial districts. Spike. Using the #253 land-use classes, try per-class defaults by hand and with a throwaway prototype where cheap, reusing lib/layers/outbuildings.py for sheds and feature_build.py for larger massing: yard and car-park surfaces, fence and gate lines, loading bays, simple shed and warehouse massing with lidar height, shop frontages and awnings, forecourts, signage as plain colour blocks. Compare variants by what a player sees from the street. Deliver findings in docs/plans/industrial-commercial.md: which defaults carry the vibe, which evidence exists for them anywhere in the UK (OSM tags, aerial), cost in minutes and session tokens (method stated), a recommended defaults table for the #253 classes retail/commercial, industrial and car park, and follow-up tasks to file from the findings. Scratch effects and snags go to the named world's repo. Check: findings file has a Cost heading and recommended-table rows; the owner's in-game verdict is recorded in it.

tasks.title: Trial: park and rural patch (owner picks study areas)
tasks.notes: NEEDS USER INPUT: the owner names the world, a park with paths and pitches and a rural patch with fields, hedges and woodland (water or coast welcome if close), and says whether they may be rebuilt. Plan: docs/plans/vibe-at-scale.md section 6. Owner direction 2026-11-10: any UK place, so open land matters. Spike. Using the #253 classes, try defaults by hand and with a throwaway prototype where cheap: field boundaries (hedge, fence, gate), path surfaces, pitch markings, woodland edge and scrub, grass colour variation, ponds and streams via the water_body feature (#163), bench and lamp placement from OSM points or labelled inference. Compare variants by what a player sees walking through and from a hill. Deliver findings in docs/plans/park-rural.md: recommended defaults rows for the park/leisure, farmland/rural and woodland classes, which evidence exists UK-wide and where it is thin (sparse OSM; height source outside England unverified), cost in minutes and session tokens (method stated), and follow-up tasks to file from the findings. Scratch effects and snags go to the named world's repo. Check: findings file has a Cost heading and recommended-row table; the owner's in-game verdict is recorded in it.

tasks.title: Tidy the nits from the #301, #302, #303 and #304 reviews (float-height fallback, terrain reports, barrier columns, ridge axis bounds)
tasks.notes:
Review nits from the #301 and #302 reviews (2026-11-16/17); no blockers, all merged. Do the first group first; the rest are optional.

From #302 (lib/builds/feature_build.py, lib/sources/lidar_provider.py):
1. `mc_heights_float` (lidar_provider.py ~167): `except TypeError` also swallows a TypeError raised inside the provider's float path and silently re-runs the integer sample, so roofs quietly return to whole metres; a caller that passes its own float keyword also hits a duplicate-keyword TypeError. Catch narrowly or check the signature once, and say in the report when the fallback fires.
2. `_load_zone_grids` (~1572/1577) samples the same bbox twice (whole-metre `dsm` and float `dsm_fine`); add a comment that this keeps `dsm` exactly as before.
3. `zone_ridge_half_steps` docstring (~514): say NaN in `med` means no-data and is dropped from `readable` and the neighbour cap.
4. Second repair loop (~632-634): the cliff-cap pass can bring back a lone odd cell on the last pass, with no re-check after the loop; add a test with a deeper steep hip.
5. Ridge rows must not jog (#302 item 3): only a synthetic test guards it (`test_noisy_float_ridge_plans_no_ridge_jog_and_no_lone_slab`); add one that fails without the smoothing, or state it is covered by the dry-run check.
6. test_feature_build.py `SmoothRoofHalfStepsTest` reuses another class's fixtures via `PitchedZonesFloatDsmTest('test_whole_metre...').setUp()`; use a shared helper or mixin. Design note: flattening drops lone 1-half-step cells instead of calibrating the deck offset; ridge heights stay lidar-absolute (acceptable; record in the commit).

From #301 (lib/layers/trees_layer.py, decor_layer.py):
7. `report['terrain']` counts (`used`, `moved`, `fallback`) only reach the JSON report; print them in the console run summary, and count decor columns that fell back to the live surface where terrain is missing (change point 7).
8. `cell_terrain` (trees_layer.py ~354-364): bare `except Exception: return None` silently reverts every tree to the old roof behaviour; print a one-line warning.
9. `place_barriers_from_plan` (decor_layer.py ~454-482): a multi-high barrier column places the free parts and drops the rest, counted as placed; make it all-or-nothing or report 'feature above terrain' (existed before #301).
10. trees_layer.py ~617: comment why `fallback=surface_y` is passed (tests patch it).
11. `may_join_at` (decor_layer.py ~739-744): joins have no ground check, so a join across a gap or water could be placed in the air (intended, tested by `test_join_pieces_has_no_terrain_veto`); decide whether to keep.

Check: `python3 scripts/run_tests.py --only test_feature_build --only test_lidar_provider --only test_trees_layer --only test_decor_layer`; dry runs unchanged for west_w34391673, w146985470, w33830050 and cell 48,-44. Group 1 touches feature_build.py, so serialise with #304 (pitched ridge caps, same file).

From the #303 review (2026-11-19, merged, no blockers): (a) lib/layers/test_trees_layer.py: the TestDryRunUndo class sits after `if __name__ == '__main__'`, so a direct file run skips it; move it above. (b) decor_layer.py and trees_layer.py dry runs pass modifies=(*ignored_builds(cell), name); add a one-line comment saying the simulated undo needs it. (c) lib/layers/layer_planning.py: with no own mask the helper still wraps the world in PlannedWorld; it could return the world unwrapped.

From the #304 review (2026-11-19, merged, no blockers): (d) lib/builds/feature_build.py roof_ridge_runs: if the narrow axis is not bounded by lower cells the loop falls through to the longer axis and can still qualify the run (a 2x1 plateau with missing z flanks but lower x flanks becomes a 2-wide stair pair); the ticket says the narrow axis must be bounded, so return no width when it fails, with a test. (e) The 1x1 apex only checks the x axis; check both. (f) Rename the loop variable `delta` unpacked as dx, dz so it does not shadow the outer names.

tasks.notes:
Spike. Question from the owner (handoff 2026-11-19, after #306): do decor furniture reads need finer than z20 aerial? The 48,-44 designer reading (reference/decor-furniture.json, 2026-10-27) listed 22 bicycle_parking and 3 bench items and missed the picnic tables the aerial shows (I-008, S-033).

Change: none to code. Compare the picnic-table and bench sites of 48,-44 at z20 and one finer zoom, plus street view where available, then answer: does a finer zoom change what a designer reads, and what does it cost (tile count, fetch size, provider limits)? Use whatever imagery types the active world has; ask for a type, never a vendor (third-party providers are the owner's own installs).

Check: a short note in docs/specs/ with a table of the sites compared, what each zoom showed, the cost, and a yes/no recommendation. Docs only; commit to main. A yes becomes its own task; do not implement here.

Not world work: the re-read and decor redo of 48,-44 stay with the builds thread.

tasks.title: Pitched roof terrace edges: stairs or slabs instead of full-block rises (I-019 S-086)
tasks.notes:
Issue: Pitched roofs built from full blocks, no stairs or slabs (I-019), owner snag S-086 (west_w34391673): "using slabs but there's still places there's a full block rise when steps or slabs would be better". I-019 stage: pitched roof terrace edges (full block with no higher neighbour).

Before starting: #304 (ridge caps) and #300/#302 (float heights, smoothing) changed pitched_roof_states in lib/builds/feature_build.py. Re-run a dry run of West on current main and count full-block rises with a lower neighbour that a stair or slab would fit; if #304 already covers them, close this as already done.

Cause (read from code, not verified in game): a terrace edge is a cell with a lower neighbour and no higher neighbour; pitched_roof_states gives a stair only where a neighbour is at least 2 half-steps higher, so such an edge gets a full block. Settle with a half-height grid dump of the West roof before choosing a rule.

Change: a rule for terrace edges (stair, slab or full block by the height step and what is beside it), with unit tests on small height grids in lib/builds/test_feature_build.py, including a case the existing stair and slab rules must not change.

Check: python3 scripts/run_tests.py --only test_feature_build passes; a dry run of West shows fewer full-block rises beside a lower cell. After a rebuild, the owner reviews S-086 in game (world work). On landing: the orchestrator logs the fix on I-019 with a check line for every open snag.

tasks.title: Diagnose grey quarter squares behind roof stairs (I-022 S-087)
tasks.notes:
Issue: Roof stairs ignore neighbours and rotation, leaving gaps (I-022), owner snag S-087 (west_w34391673): "I can see grey 1/4 squares where I am looking right now". The earlier fix F-1 (#169) is withdrawn.

Diagnosis first (this task is the diagnosis; fix as a follow-up unless it is a one-line change). Not verified in the issue: which block shows as grey quarter squares behind the stairs. Candidates: the wall fill under a stair column (edge_wall_expose, about lib/builds/feature_build.py:1588-1595, treats a stair as a full block), the open half of a stair looking into air or an interior block, or the game rewriting a stair's corner shape from same-height neighbours. Steps: dump blocks around the snag position (registry/issues/img/S-087.png and the snag's pos), identify the grey block, and say which code path put it there.

Change: after the cause is named, fix it with a unit test for the exact column pattern; do not widen to the stair shape and facing rule (I-022's other stages) unless the cause is the same.

Check: python3 scripts/run_tests.py --only test_feature_build passes; a block scan of the snag site after a rebuild shows no grey block behind the stairs (world work). On landing: the orchestrator logs the fix on I-022 with a check line for S-029, S-051, S-065 and S-087.

tasks.title: Flat roof areas built with stairs that gain no height (I-048 S-088)
tasks.notes:
Issue: Flat roof areas are built with stairs that gain no height (I-048), owner snag S-088 (west_w34391673): "the flat black roof uses stairs without gaining height".

Verified in the live world 2026-11-19: polished-deepslate stairs run along x6156-6181 at z-5640 and again at z-5639, both at y58, all facing south (straight), so two adjacent rows at the same height face the same way and climb nowhere.

Cause not established. pitched_roof_states (lib/builds/feature_build.py ~823) gives a stair only where a neighbour is at least 2 half-steps higher, so a flat deck should not get stairs from that path. Candidates: the dark zone (level 47) height grid had a ramp that was flattened after the stairs were chosen, or another path places them (a zone-material boundary, edge rows, or a hip eave). Step one: dump the half-height grid for west_w34391673 around x6156-6181, z-5640 and see.

Before starting: #304 touches the same function; re-run on current main first and close as already done if the stairs are gone.

Change: remove the cause, with a unit test of a flat deck beside the offending boundary that expects no stairs.

Check: python3 scripts/run_tests.py --only test_feature_build passes; a dry run of West plans no stairs on the flat dark zone. After a rebuild the owner reviews S-088 in game (world work). On landing: the orchestrator logs the fix on I-048 with a check line for S-088.

tasks.title: Bounded-window policy drops nearly all glass on a mass rotated 25-30 degrees (SUSU)
tasks.notes:
Found while reviewing glazing after the #192 facade_plan glazing change (reported to the owner 2026-11-19; the figures are from that report, not re-measured here): the bounded-window policy (lib/builds/window_openings.py `choose_windows`, which resolves every intended opening against the finished shell and refuses ones without structural jambs, exposure or known outside ground) drops nearly all glass on a mass rotated about 25-30 degrees, the SUSU building (susu_w33830305).

Cause: NOT established. Working hypothesis only: on a rotated mass the stair-stepped shell has no straight 1-block-deep jamb runs on the N/S/E/W faces, so the structural, exposed and outside_ground tests refuse most openings. To do first: run the window selection read-only on the recorded SUSU shell (no builder dry run; the live world is not needed if the journal or build spec holds the shell), list the refusal reasons per face from `report_lines`, and say which test refuses and why.

Deliverable: either glass on rotated masses at a rate close to the facade_plan glazing rows, or a clear per-face report that says how much was dropped and why. Choose after the read-only count. Axis-aligned masses must not change (a test).

Related: the glazing-rows issue (I-030, confirmed, fix #192 logged) stays OPEN until the EEE glazed-share comparison is re-run by the owner; this task does not close it. No world registry writes from the implementer; the orchestrator logs any fix on the issue found for SUSU.
Do not: run builds, undo, redo or live-world commands; take the site lock; change anything under worlds/.
Check: the read-only count on SUSU shows glazed share within a stated tolerance of its facade_plan rows (tolerance chosen after the count), and python3 scripts/run_tests.py --only test_window_openings passes if that test exists (otherwise name the new test file).
